New Features: Post-clip: ClipEm can keep recording for a few seconds after you press the clip hotkey, so you catch what's said right after. Turn it on in Setup or Settings > Clip Output. Your clip saves as usual, along with a "-extra.mkv" copy that has the extra seconds.
In the clip editor, a clip with a post-clip copy opens ending at the hotkey press. Use Include extra, or drag the end handle, to keep the extra seconds.
Clip naming lets you choose the post-clip copy's suffix.
Release notes: see what's new before and after updating, and every version's notes in Settings.
Read every ClipEm log, OBS log and OBS crash report in Settings, with View Logs in Troubleshooting.
Improvements: On Windows and Linux, OBS now stays fully out of sight: ClipEm's tray icon is the only one, and OBS's errors and messages appear as ClipEm notifications.
Settings and the clip editor have their own icons.
Settings has a new Recording/Devices tab and reorganized boxes.
The ClipEm Is Already Open window can now kill a stuck ClipEm and OBS and start fresh.
Stuck-screen detection now leaves a screen alone when nothing is happening on it, so fewer false alarms.
If OBS crashes, ClipEm now tells you and restarts it.
Fixes: OBS no longer checks for missing files at startup, a dialog nobody could see with OBS hidden.
If ClipEm loses access to your screen on Linux, it now opens the screen picker itself instead of asking you to fix it in OBS.

New Features: Missing-mic detection: ClipEm notices when your mic isn't reaching clips and fixes it, or tells you.
Choose what saved clips and their copies are called, in Setup and Settings.
Choose the video encoder, including hardware encoders, in Setup and Settings.
Start/stop hotkeys for recording and the replay buffer.
A Pick... button that sets a hotkey by pressing it.
Settings for the audio peak guard and OBS script debug messages, with "i" buttons explaining options.
Improvements: Setup has new pages for clip names and hotkeys, shows a screenshot of the clip editor, and continues on its own after a step finishes.
All popups are a standard size, including file pickers on Linux.
The replay buffer's memory limit now follows its length and bitrate, so long clips aren't cut short.
Recorded audio moved from 160 to 192 kbps.
Updated the bundled Python from 3.12.10 to 3.12.16 on Windows, and from 3.12.14 to 3.12.16 on Linux.
Updated Electron, which runs the clip editor's window, from 44.5.1 to 44.9.3.
Updated Pillow from 12.3.0 to 13.0.0.

New Features: The tray widget now records each app that makes sound itself, and gives it a track in the clip's multitrack copy automatically.
New dark theme across Setup and Settings.
Settings > UI Customization, with a color picker.
Clip sound presets: Scissors, the new default, and Flash.
Clip editor: master volume, a level meter, and a button that levels out every track at once.
Choose which folder the clip editor shows clips from.
Improvements: ClipEm now uses your system's file and folder pickers where it can.
Clip editor sliders have new controls, and volumes can be typed in dB.
Fixes: Per-app tracks on Windows now use ClipEm's own capture helper.

New Features: Crop clips in the clip editor, with zoom controls.
Improvements: The clip editor reopens by itself if it was open during an update or restart.
Quitting and restarting from the tray now leaves the right things running.
Fixes: Scrolling the page no longer changes a dropdown under the pointer.
Fixed sidebar size and UI scaling.

New Features: Choose ClipEm's editor or your own external editor, or turn clip editors off.
Choose whether the tray menu shows Start Recording.
Improvements: Exports show which clip they came from, with a link back to it.
Level Out Audio now handles track volume changes better.
The clip editor's noise gate has a strength control, and sets itself between the noise and speech levels.

New Features: Settings can now change the replay buffer length, recording bitrate, audio devices and mic filter, as Setup can.
Settings can now change the smaller copy of each clip, and which apps own which audio tracks, with Pin and Reset.
Clip editor effects per track: Level, Noise gate and Mono.
Volume changes can apply to just the left or right channel: hold Alt while dragging on a stereo track.
Play an export, or show it in its folder, right after exporting.
Optional notification when a clip is saved from the tray menu.
Improvements: The tray menu is dark on Windows.
Windows notifications are now named ClipEm on installs that updated.
Settings now shows the update source as a GitHub link.
Update channel is now called Update branch, with Main and Dev.

New Features: The full clip editor, in its own window: trim, delete sections, edit per-track audio, resize the video and tracks, and export.
Send Bug Report: send logs and a description without a GitHub account.
Delete clips from the clip editor's list.
An application menu entry on Linux.
Improvements: The tray widget is now always installed, and starts at boot alongside OBS.
The default smaller-copy target moved from 10 to 20 MB, Discord's new limit.
Linux OBS now includes per-app audio capture.
App tracks with no sound in a clip are left out of it.
Fixes: Fixed exiting, restarting and autostart behavior.

New Features: Clip Browser: browse your clips, hover to play them with sound, and open them in an editor.
Split audio tracks: an optional "-tracks.mkv" copy of each clip with separate audio tracks.
Optional LosslessCut download for quick trims, or use your own editor.
Reinstall ClipEm from Settings, keeping or resetting your settings.
Create a bug report zip from Settings.
Update channel and update source settings.
Install and Uninstall Autostart buttons in Settings.
A Start Menu entry on Windows.
Improvements: Updates now come from GitHub releases.
The tray warns when the clips folder is missing, and can create it again.

New Features: Offline installs: the bundles include everything, so installing needs no internet.
ClipEm now asks before updating, and can update OBS, the bundled Python and the tray's packages as well as itself.
Install an update now or at the next restart, or skip it.
Improvements: Setup shows step numbers and has an Updates page.
A warning when ClipEm is already running, with Proceed Anyway.

New Features: Low disk space and large recording warnings, with a setting to turn them off.

Fixes: Fixed package installs on Windows installs made over an older Python.

New Features: Hide OBS from the tray, which now shows Show OBS or Hide OBS as needed.

Improvements: The Settings window closes along with the tray widget.
Clip Hotkey is now the first section in Settings.

Fixes: Quitting the tray no longer leaves a python3 process running in the background.

Improvements: Settings has separate Scripts and OBS Websocket sections, and a button to show the password.

New Features: Clip sound settings: turn it on or off, set its volume, choose your own .wav, and preview it.

Fixes: Restarting a PipeWire screen capture now works, by pressing Select Monitor on OBS's main thread.

Improvements: ClipEm retries when a PipeWire screen capture stays dead, and treats a capture with no picture as stuck.

New Features: Restart ClipEm Tray and OBS, in the tray menu.
Dead PipeWire screen captures are restarted, with a prompt to pick your screen.

Fixes: The tray reconnects properly when OBS restarts, picking up new websocket settings.

New Features: Black-screen detection, with a setting to turn it on.
Improvements: Capture recovery points the capture back at your chosen display.
Stuck-screen detection reacts sooner: 5 identical checks in a row instead of 10.
Fixes: Fixed Linux notifications failing with some notification servers.

Improvements: More detailed logging from the stuck-screen check.
Moved Settings further down the tray menu.
Stuck-screen detection moved from an OBS script to the tray widget, so its setting can change any time.
The audio peak guard reacts within 1 dB of full scale, and its ceiling can be set.
Show OBS works better on KDE.

Fixes: Installs that still had the developer's clip folder from releases up to 1.2.7 now get the default folder.

New Features: Show OBS from the tray on Windows and Linux.
A Copy button for the websocket password.
Improvements: Renamed the quit options to Quit ClipEm Tray Only and Quit ClipEm Tray and OBS.
Removing other ClipEm autostart entries in Setup is now opt-in.

New Features: Audio peak guard: turns down audio sources that are clipping.
Setup finds and offers to remove autostart entries from other ClipEm folders.
Ctrl+A, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Shift+R in every text field.
Improvements: Setup and other windows use the ClipEm logo.
The Settings window uses the ClipEm logo, and groups as ClipEm in the taskbar.

Fixes: The Windows installer now asks you to close ClipEm or OBS and retry, when they're running from the install folder.

Improvements: Updated OBS from 31.0.2 to 32.2.2 on Windows and macOS.
OBS's Windows debug symbols, about 76 MB, are no longer installed.

New Features: Set the clip hotkey and websocket port and password in Settings, applied the next time OBS starts.
ClipEm downloads OBS again if it's missing, instead of failing.
Improvements: Setup closes OBS before starting, because OBS would overwrite its changes.
Only one copy of the tray widget can run.
Updated the Linux Python from 3.12.11 to 3.12.14.
Updated Tcl/Tk from 8.6.16 to 9.0.4 on Linux.
Setup now asks for a recording bitrate instead of a target file size, and it follows the resolution unless you've set your own.
Fixes: ClipEm no longer leaves a console window on Windows that killed the tray widget when closed.
Quit ClipEm + OBS on Windows now stops OBS's outputs first and closes the right OBS window.

Improvements: Setup now scales properly on high-DPI displays.

Fixes: Display Capture now points at your primary display on fresh Windows installs, instead of showing "Device not connected".

Improvements: Setup warns on Windows if the Visual C++ runtime OBS needs is missing.

Fixes: More reliable Tk install on Windows, so Setup's window appears, with detailed logging.
Fixed pip refusing to install on Windows.
Fixed update checks failing with 403 Forbidden from clipem.app.
Fixed Setup failing to start on Windows, where its own folder wasn't on Python's path.

New Features: Save a smaller copy of each clip ("-small.mp4"), sized for upload limits, with ffmpeg installed for it. The original is always kept.
Updates are now verified with a release signature.
Autostart settings for OBS and the tray widget.
A Check for Updates button in Settings.
